svg.title: SMOOTHIE CENTRAL — external connectors and internal Core P1 connections
svg.desc: Four-sided Core P1 wiring diagram with 82 exterior contacts, XYZA motor control, 90 numbered Gadgeteer contacts in nine five-column cards, a compact color and symbol key, a filtered Gadgeteer socket-type table, and the complete 40-contact motor-header pinout.
svg.metadata: Core P1 schematic and exported netlist identify board connector, transistor and rail paths; the laser buffer and MOSFET stages are proposed external carrier circuitry, not fitted Core parts. The diode array groups three separate ideal-diode stages, not a claimed fitted array package; selection depends on available voltage subject to stage drops and limits, not wattage. USB reaches /5V only after its own U18 limiter. Matching 5 V SOURCE and TO ALL 5V flags denote /5V, available at J43.1; J35.2 is a separate limited branch. Core 5 V source priority and output load budget are unverified. Machine axes X/Y/Z/A rename the former A/B/C/D harness roles without changing J5 contacts or MCU pins; SG_A/SG_B/SG_C/SG_D remain the source net identities. Motor J5 pinout is source-number order, not a physical mating-face view. Gadgeteer capability letters are inferred by comparison with Microsoft .NET Gadgeteer Socket Types Table v16 and do not establish module or firmware compatibility. FET limit pills are conditional datasheet values. Connector pills describe proposed Phoenix Contact 1733729 nominal 630 V and 24 A only. Neither is an assembled-board or harness rating. FET glyph adapts KiCad Transistor_FET; ground glyph adapts Tabler circuit-ground (MIT). Source references stay in data attributes for audit, not visible labels.

svg.text: Showing external connectors of the Smoothie-central setup and how they internally connect to a Smoothie v2-core
The high-side switch feeds four FET_CUT positives; bed control is on VFET.
* Device limits apply at datasheet conditions; board and harness limits remain unqualified.
Highest available voltage, subject to stage drops/limits — not highest wattage.
Fitted behavior and load budget unverified; limited header branches remain separate.
Gate low: output high; gate high: off.
Output-low bias and driver polarity: TBD.
Motor source key: columns X / Y / Z / A; rows STEP / DIR / EN; numbers are header contacts, not the physical two-row layout.
Separate EN proposals replace StallGuard inputs; shared EN is unused. GPIO assignments and laser polarity require configuration and validation.
P/N name transistor channels; the servo has a 10 kΩ pull-up. Laser PWM/TTL are signals, not laser power or a safety interlock.
External laser stages use 5 V SOURCE flags from the accessory output; the 5V LIMITED field contact stays separate. All signal GNDs are common.
5 V SOURCE / TO ALL 5V name the same board supply; LIMITED is separate. Dots join; pale crossing gaps do not.
Dark pill ends name contacts; black/white limits are voltage/current. * Device or candidate-connector limits do not rate the assembly.
Socket ID GA–GI and capability type A/I/P/S/Y are different labels. Type letters describe pin capabilities, not plug-and-play firmware support.
GB_4, GB_5, GD_4 and GD_5 are expansion nets without a direct MCU ball in this schematic; GND means circuit return.
Source-number order; not the physical mating-face orientation.
† SG_A–D serve proposed X/Y/Z/A ENABLE paths; shared MOT_EN is unused in this harness. Firmware must configure this choice.
Shared pins: 1 = 3.3 V · 2 = 5 V · 10 = GND. Cells show pins 3–9.
! = interrupt-capable GPIO; (G) = GPIO alternate; — = unused. COPI/CIPO correspond to the standard's MOSI/MISO.
S uses a pin-6 GPIO as chip select when configured. Letter matches indicate pin capability, not a tested module.
